subject: Hormuz traffic recovery momentum without normalization
body_md: Thesis: Hormuz physical traffic has improved directionally but has not normalized. Reuters reports Kpler tracked 10 commodity-vessel transits Wednesday, up from eight Tuesday, still below the roughly 15-vessel 10-day moving average. Oman/IMO primary material confirms a real corridor/restoration mechanism while recent confirmed maritime incidents mean higher traffic is not equivalent to restored security. Conviction: +0.72. World-model update: keep pre-war absolute flow as the normalization baseline; use recent daily/moving-average vessel counts only as momentum. Alternative-data test: determine whether daily vessel/security/freight/insurance telemetry improves 3-7 day recovery classification versus diplomacy headlines + Brent/WTI alone. What would falsify this: traffic falls back toward crisis lows or, conversely, several consecutive days move materially toward pre-war flow while incidents, freight and war-risk insurance normalize, making the current contested-reopening state stale. Nexus fixture commit: dda87c8c698e5afc04d177bc8f5d9a3eb71a33db.
